items.stem: The board has approved the ------- of two additional distribution centres in the eastern region.
items.explain_en: Between “the” and “of” a noun is required: “the construction of”.

items.stem: By the time the auditors arrive next Monday, the finance team ------- all supporting documents.
items.explain_en: “By the time” with a future reference (“next Monday”) calls for the future perfect: the work will be complete before the auditors arrive.

items.stem: Mr. Halloran has worked at Brightline Logistics ------- more than fifteen years.
items.explain_en: “for” introduces a duration (fifteen years); “since” would introduce a starting point, as in “since 2011”.

items.stem: The revised safety guidelines ------- to all warehouse personnel last Thursday.
items.explain_en: The guidelines are distributed, they do not distribute: past passive, consistent with “last Thursday”.

items.stem: Sales in the northern territory grew ------- after the advertising campaign was launched.
items.explain_en: The word modifies the verb “grew”, so an adverb is needed.
items.qc_fix: grew sharply：副词修饰动词；原缺语法节点

items.stem: ------- the renovation took longer than planned, the restaurant reopened on schedule.
items.explain_en: The two clauses contrast — the work overran, yet the restaurant reopened on time — which calls for the concessive “Although”.

items.stem: We are looking for a supplier ------- delivery times are consistently under three days.
items.explain_en: The delivery times belong to the supplier, so the possessive relative “whose” is required.

items.stem: Employees should log out of the system before ------- the building.
items.explain_en: Here “before” acts as a preposition, so the verb that follows takes the -ing form.

items.stem: The list of approved contractors ------- updated at the end of every quarter.
items.explain_en: The subject is “the list”, which is singular; “of approved contractors” is only a modifier. A classic agreement trap.

items.stem: The revised layout makes the assembly line considerably ------- than the previous one.
items.explain_en: “than” requires a comparative, and because “efficient” is a long adjective it forms one with “more”.

items.stem: Please ------- the attached invoice to your accounting department for processing.
items.explain_en: “forward something to someone” means to pass it on. “proceed” and “arrive” are intransitive, and “promote” does not carry that sense.

items.stem: The technicians completed the installation ------- without any assistance from the vendor.
items.explain_en: An emphatic reflexive pronoun: they did it themselves.

items.stem: Ms. Ibarra travelled to the Rotterdam plant ------- the new packaging equipment.
items.explain_en: Infinitive of purpose: she travelled in order to inspect the equipment.

items.stem: Applicants with ------- experience in freight forwarding will be given priority.
items.explain_en: “proven” is a past participle used as an adjective: demonstrated experience.
items.qc_fix: with proven experience：名词前分词形容词，不是动词位

items.stem: If the shipment ------- delayed again, we will have to notify the client immediately.
items.explain_en: First conditional: present tense in the “if” clause, future in the main clause.

items.stem: ------- of the participants left before the closing remarks, so the room remained full until the end.
items.explain_en: “Few” goes with a plural countable noun and carries the negative sense that “so the room remained full” requires.

items.stem: The consultant's recommendations were both practical and -------.
items.explain_en: “both … and …” links two elements of the same kind, so after the adjective “practical” another adjective is needed.

items.stem: All of our offices will be closed ------- 25 December for the winter holiday.
items.explain_en: “on” is used before a specific date; “in” goes with months and years, “at” with clock times.

items.stem: Visitors ------- wear an identification badge at all times while on the factory floor.
items.explain_en: “at all times” signals an absolute obligation, so “must”. The other modals express mere possibility.

items.stem: Because of a scheduling -------, two departments reserved the same room for Tuesday afternoon.
items.explain_en: “scheduling conflict” is the set collocation for two bookings that overlap.
items.qc_fix: scheduling conflict 名词词义（选项形近）；原缺词汇节点

items.stem: Since ------- the sales team in 2019, Ms. Delacroix has doubled her regional revenue.
items.explain_en: “Since” followed by a verb with no expressed subject takes the -ing form.

items.stem: All expense claims ------- by a department manager before payment is issued.
items.explain_en: The claims are approved, they do not approve: passive after a modal, “must be + past participle”.

items.stem: The company installed additional lighting ------- the parking area would be safer at night.
items.explain_en: “so that” introduces a full clause with its own subject and verb; “in order to” would be followed by an infinitive.

items.stem: The programme is designed to ------- new hires with the company's safety procedures.
items.explain_en: After “to”, the bare infinitive is required: “familiarize someone with something”.

items.stem: The Hartwell Building, ------- was completed in 1998, will undergo a full renovation next spring.
items.explain_en: A non-defining relative clause between commas with an inanimate antecedent takes “which”; “that” cannot follow a comma.

items.stem: ------- of the two remaining candidates holds the required certification, so we will reopen the search.
items.explain_en: The sense is negative — the search is being reopened — and there are only two candidates, so “Neither”, agreeing in the singular with “holds”. “None” would imply at least three.

items.stem: Ridgeway Consulting has built a strong ------- for delivering projects ahead of schedule.
items.explain_en: “build a reputation for doing something” is the expected collocation.

items.stem: ------- in a plain envelope, the contract arrived without attracting any attention.
items.explain_en: The contract undergoes the action of being sent, so a past participle opens the sentence, equivalent to “Because it was sent…”.

items.stem: The manager praised the team for its careful ------- to detail throughout the audit.
items.explain_en: After the adjective “careful” a noun is needed, and “attention to detail” is itself a set phrase.

items.stem: Neither the supervisor nor the assistants ------- aware of the change in procedure.
items.explain_en: With “neither … nor …” the verb agrees with the second subject, here the plural “the assistants”. The past context rules out the present tense.
Future passive: “will no longer be accepted” — the paper forms will stop being taken.

options: This removes the need to keep printed copies for your records.
Paper receipts must still be mailed to the finance office.
The portal can be accessed only from computers inside the building.
Reimbursement rates have been revised for the coming year.
items.explain_en: The previous sentence explains that receipts are photographed, so the logical consequence is that no paper copies need keeping. Still mailing paper receipts, or restricting the portal to office computers, would contradict the paragraph.
The subject “we” needs a finite present-tense verb: “we strongly recommend it”.
items.qc_fix: we strongly recommend：主语+副词后缺谓语动词；原缺语法节点

items.explain_en: After the possessive determiner “your”, a singular uncountable noun is needed: “your patience”.
The word modifies the adjectival phrase “out of stock”, so an adverb is needed.

options: We are therefore able to offer an alternative model in the same price range.
Your payment has been refunded in full.
The chairs were unfortunately delivered to the wrong address.
Our showroom is open seven days a week.
items.explain_en: The next sentence opens with “It is identical in design”, so the pronoun requires that a replacement model has just been introduced.
“waive a charge” means to drop it — the only sense compatible with “as a gesture of goodwill”.
A present-tense closing formula: “We appreciate your understanding”.
A certain future consequence of an instruction: “will be placed”. “would” would imply an unreal hypothesis.
items.qc_fix: will + be placed：句内即可判断（are/were 后不能接 be），不是语境时态

options: This is a good opportunity to reduce the volume of material you store.
The fourth floor has just been completely renovated.
The movers will pack your personal belongings for you.
The relocation has been postponed until July.
items.explain_en: The next sentence invites people to discard what they no longer need, so the paragraph must open on sorting. Having the movers pack for you contradicts the labelling instruction, and a July postponement contradicts the memo's own dates.
“accept responsibility for something”: after the verb, the singular uncountable noun is required.
After a future-referring “when”, English uses the present tense, never “will”.
items.qc_fix: when you arrive：时间从句现在代将来，句内可判

items.explain_en: After the verb “is”, a predicative adjective is needed: “is eligible to apply”.
“priority” undergoes the action, so the passive: “priority is given to”.

options: Every application must include a written endorsement from your line manager.
The grant may also be used towards personal travel.
Applications are accepted at any time during the year.
The programme was suspended for the whole of last year.
items.explain_en: “Applications submitted without one” requires that a single mandatory item has just been mentioned — the manager's endorsement. Accepting applications year-round would contradict the April and October rounds.
“take something seriously”: the adverb modifies the verb, in the passive as much as the active.

items.stem: Vessel arrivals at Terminal 4 are posted hourly so that hauliers can plan their collections more -------.
items.explain_en: “Plan” is a verb, so it takes an adverb: “plan their collections more accurately”.

items.stem: By the time the new sorting hub opens in March, the company ------- more than €4 million in automation.
items.explain_en: “By the time” plus a future event calls for the future perfect: the investing will be complete before the hub opens.

items.stem: All catering orders must be confirmed ------- writing at least seventy-two hours before the event.
items.explain_en: The fixed expression is “in writing”, meaning in a written document.

items.stem: The banquet hall can be arranged in several ------- depending on the size of the party.
items.explain_en: “Several” must be followed by a plural noun: “several configurations”.

items.stem: The publisher decided to ------- the launch of the biography until the author's tour dates were confirmed.
items.explain_en: “Postpone … until” is the only choice that means moving an event to a later date, which is what the unconfirmed tour dates require.

items.stem: Damaged pallets ------- from the container before the shipment was released to the customer.
items.explain_en: The pallets receive the action, so a past passive is needed to match “was released”.

items.stem: Guests staying more than five nights receive a ------- discount on all spa treatments.
items.explain_en: An adjective is needed before the noun “discount”: “a substantial discount”.

items.stem: The freight forwarder recommends ------- perishable goods at least a week before the holiday period.
items.explain_en: “Recommend” takes a gerund when no object follows it: “recommends booking”.

items.stem: ------- the ferry crossing was delayed by fog, the delegates arrived in time for the opening reception.
items.explain_en: The delay and the on-time arrival conflict, so a concessive conjunction is required. “Because” would make the delay the reason they were punctual.

items.stem: The hotel's night manager handled the double-booking with impressive -------.
items.explain_en: After the preposition “with” and the adjective “impressive”, a noun is required: “with impressive composure”.

items.stem: Ms. Adeyemi ------- the conference centre's audiovisual team since it was founded eight years ago.
items.explain_en: “Since” with a past starting point calls for the present perfect, showing that she still leads the team.

items.stem: The distribution centre ------- we visited last month processes 12,000 parcels an hour.
items.explain_en: “Visited” has no object, so the relative pronoun fills that gap. “Where” is tempting because the noun is a place, but it would leave “visited” incomplete.

items.stem: Please ensure that the invoice number is printed ------- on the outside of every carton.
items.explain_en: An adverb is needed to modify the verb “is printed”: “printed legibly”.

items.stem: The trade fair stand must be dismantled ------- midnight on Sunday.
items.explain_en: “By” marks a deadline for a single completed action; “until” would describe an activity continuing up to midnight.

items.stem: Bookshops that return unsold copies within ninety days are eligible for a full -------.
items.explain_en: Money returned for goods sent back is a refund; a “reduction” would lower a future price rather than repay one already paid.
items.qc_fix: a full refund 名词词义；原缺词汇节点

items.stem: The catering manager praised the kitchen staff for their ------- under pressure.
items.explain_en: The praise is for a quality the staff showed, and “professionalism” is the noun naming it. “Profession” would mean their trade, not their conduct.

items.stem: The list of approved freight carriers ------- reviewed by the procurement committee each quarter.
items.explain_en: The subject is the singular “list”, not the plural “carriers” inside the prepositional phrase.

items.stem: When the courier arrived at the loading bay, the warehouse team ------- already sealed the last crate.
items.explain_en: The sealing happened before the past arrival, so the past perfect is required.

items.stem: Delegates found the keynote speaker's account of the industry's transformation deeply -------.
items.explain_en: The account produces the effect, so the present participle is used; “fascinated” would describe the delegates, not the account.

items.stem: The hotel group announced the ------- of three boutique properties on the Adriatic coast.
items.explain_en: Between “the” and “of” only a noun can stand: “the acquisition of”.

items.stem: ------- of the two banquet rooms has its own service entrance.
items.explain_en: The singular verb “has” and the singular “its” rule out “both”, which would take “have”. “Every” cannot be followed by “of”.

items.stem: The revised distribution agreement ------- by both parties before the end of the fiscal year.
items.explain_en: The agreement is what gets signed, and the agent appears in a “by” phrase, so the modal passive is required.

EASTVALE (2 November) — The Eastvale Transit Authority will shorten Route 42 from 14 December, ending the service at Fenwick Interchange rather than continuing to Marley Green. Deputy director Hana Vogel said the change would let the authority add two morning departures on Route 42 itself, where crowding has been the subject of repeated complaints. "We are moving capacity to where the passengers are," she said.

The authority held two public meetings in September. Attendance was low — nineteen people in total — a fact critics attribute to the meetings' 2 P.M. start.

docs.title: Letter to the editor
docs.text:
To the Editor,

Your report on Route 42 repeated the transit authority's figure of eleven passengers a day without asking how it was produced.

I have used the Marley Green stop for nine years. The count was taken in the first week of August, when the packing plant that employs most of us shuts for its annual holiday. In any other week the 7:10 service alone carries fifteen to twenty of us.

I do not dispute that the two extra morning departures are needed; the buses from Fenwick are genuinely overcrowded. But the replacement minibus runs hourly, and my shift starts at 6:45 A.M. An hourly service that does not begin until seven is not a replacement — it is a removal.

As for the public meetings, I would gently point out that a two o'clock meeting on a Tuesday is not accessible to people who work shifts. That is presumably why nineteen people came.

Constance Ebele
Marley Green

KOLVIK, 3 May — Nordhaven Intermodal today opened its fourth inland terminal, a 24-hectare rail-served facility 40 kilometres south of the port of Aalgard.

Regional forwarders have given a guarded welcome to the container terminal that opened at Kolvik last week. The six-day shuttle to Aalgard was widely praised; the road gate was not.

docs.text:
Timber returns to the city centre

By Delphine Arroyo

Until recently, an eight-storey office block in this country meant steel and concrete. That is changing. Nineteen buildings of five storeys or more framed in cross-laminated timber were completed nationally last year, against three in the year the material was first permitted at that height.

Developers give two reasons. The panels arrive cut to size, so a floor can be assembled in days rather than in weeks, and a timber frame weighs roughly a fifth of a concrete one, which cuts the cost of foundations on soft ground.

Tenants appear to have noticed. Letting agents report that timber schemes are being taken up before completion at a rate the sector has not seen for a decade.

Not everyone is persuaded. Insurers have been slow to price the risk, and several city authorities still ask for fire modelling beyond what the building code requires. “The engineering is settled,” says Ravi Mahadevan of the practice Norrland & Vale. “The paperwork is not.”

MEMORANDUM

To: Design team, Studio 3
From: Ravi Mahadevan
Date: 2 April
Subject: Kesselring Quay — structure

The client has asked us to price a timber frame for Kesselring Quay alongside the concrete option and to report by the end of the month.

Two things to keep in front of us. The site is reclaimed land, so anything that lightens the building helps us at foundation level, and that argument alone may carry the decision. Sensors move into the greenhouse
By Adaeze Nwachukwu

Until recently the tomato growers of the Vale district judged their crop as their parents had: by hand, by eye, and by walking the rows twice a day. Since March, four of the district's largest producers have been running a system that does part of that walking for them.

Built by a small firm in the regional capital, the system buries a probe every twenty metres and reports soil moisture, temperature and salinity to a screen in the packing shed. Growers set a range for each figure, and when a reading leaves that range a message is sent.

The saving is not in labour. Ola Bergström, who grows twelve hectares under glass, says his staff still walk the rows. What has changed is water. “We were irrigating on a schedule,” he said. “Now we irrigate when the soil asks for it. That has cut our use by about a fifth.”

Whether smaller growers will follow is less certain. Installation runs to roughly $9,000 per hectare, and the district's co-operative has so far declined to subsidise it.

Slow trains, full carriages

Overnight rail travel across the continent, written off a decade ago as a relic, carried 4.1 million passengers last year — the highest figure since 2004. Three operators have added routes in the past eighteen months, and a fourth has ordered sleeping cars for delivery in 2028.

The revival is not driven by price. A berth from Kraków to Trieste costs €149 return, roughly twice the cheapest flight on the same day. Operators say their passengers are buying something else: a night that does not have to be spent in a hotel, and an arrival in the centre of the city that needs no onward transfer.

Load factors tell the story. On the Kraków-Trieste service, single-occupancy cabins sell out first and are typically booked eleven weeks ahead, while the ordinary seated carriages on the same train run at 62 percent.

The constraint is rolling stock. A sleeping car takes four years to build, and only two manufacturers on the continent still make them.

Visitor levy to fund coastal path
By Ingrid Sælen, 12 May

Kaldvik will introduce a visitor levy of €2.50 per guest per night from 1 October, the town council confirmed on Tuesday. The charge will apply to hotels, guesthouses and licensed short-term rentals, and will be collected by the operator and passed to the council each quarter.

Officials expect the levy to raise about €1.4 million in its first full year. Roughly two-thirds is earmarked for the long-delayed coastal path between the harbour and Storneset, with the remainder going to public toilets, waste collection and the summer shuttle bus.

Guests staying more than fourteen consecutive nights will be exempt from the fifteenth night onwards, as will anyone travelling for medical treatment.

Kaldvik recorded 310,000 overnight stays last year, 18 percent more than five years ago. Councillor Renata Bielawska, who chairs the tourism committee, said the town had “reached the point where visitors must contribute to the infrastructure they use”.

A consultation on the collection procedure closes on 30 June.

docs.title: Letter to the editor
docs.text:
To the editor,

I have run a nine-room guesthouse in Kaldvik for twenty-two years, and I am not against the levy in principle. The path your article describes has been promised since before I opened, and the state of the harbour toilets is no advertisement for us. If €2.50 a night buys those things, my guests will pay it without complaint.

My objection is to who does the collecting. Under this scheme I become an unpaid tax collector: I must add the charge, decide who is exempt, hold the money and file a return four times a year. A hotel with a finance office can absorb that. I cannot, and neither can the eleven other small operators I have spoken to.

There is an obvious alternative. The council already licenses every operator in the town. Bill the levy once a year, based on the previous year's declared occupancy, and send us a single invoice. The council collects the same money and I get my evenings back.

I would urge the committee to look at this before the consultation closes.

Halldór Jónsson
Sjøhuset Guesthouse

Small Manufacturers Share the Cost of Testing

RIVERTON (14 May) — Nineteen precision-parts makers in the Riverton industrial district have formed a cooperative to buy testing equipment that none of them could justify on its own.

The group's first purchase, a computed-tomography scanner installed in a leased unit on Kilner Road, allows a finished component to be inspected internally without being cut open. [1] Members book time on the machine through a shared calendar and are billed by the hour.

“We were each sending parts to a laboratory two hundred kilometres away and waiting nine days for a report,” said Adaeze Nwachukwu, who runs a twelve-person machine shop and chairs the cooperative. “Now it is the same afternoon.” [2]

Membership costs $4,000 a year plus usage fees. [3] The cooperative estimates that a member sending forty components a year for inspection recovers the subscription within seven months.

[4] A second unit, for surface-roughness measurement, is expected before the end of the year, and the group has opened discussions with the technical institute about using the scanner for student projects two evenings a week.
